schemeScope: Combined Ordinary scheme (12 pages; the file is named LC001GLP000EV, its text is the Irish scheme). PDF 1 cover; 2 blank; 3 general marking instruction (red ink, major errors underlined) and Páipéar I Ceist 1 composition marking (tariffs Tasc 3, Ábhar 9, Cumas Gaeilge 48 for each of two pieces, “= 60 marc × 2 = 120 marc”; the bracketed Cumas Gaeilge definition; the bracketed content note); 4 the examiner’s Nóta and a bracketed Nóta on “Gaeilge Lochtach”, then Ceist 2 reading (each question restated with one price, no answers; a 0–5 language deduction for each passage; the redundancy penalty and the closing Nóta after B); 5–9 Páipéar II; 10 the listening test; 11 Socruithe Réasúnta; 12 empty.
reviewMethod: Every paper page (1 instructions, 2 composition, 3–4 reading, 5–8 “Leathanach Bán”) and every applicable scheme page read in the text layer and checked against the printed page. The builder reads each paper page glyph by glyph by origin (2011’s reader), keeping the two passage columns apart, and asserts every prompt, title and composition line against that reading. The scheme sets its multiplication sign (PDF 3, 5–9) and its PDF 11 bullets in SymbolMT (U+F0B4, U+F0B7), read as × and •; the paper’s one SymbolMT arrow (page 1, beside “THALL”) is on no card.

nonPoolDecisions: Páipéar I before 2012 is the composition and the reading (220); the listening test is a paper of its own (irish_ordinary_2010_aural.py).

Composition: each of the nine printed titles is one 60-mark card (Tasc 3, Ábhar 9, Cumas Gaeilge 48, as the scheme prices each of the two pieces); choose-two is a choice, not a route; no combination cards. The scheme prints no 48-mark table, so Cumas Gaeilge is judged on its printed aspects.

Reading: the scheme prints no answers, only each question’s asks restated and one 10-mark price; each question is one card with one 10-mark criterion claimed whole (0 or 10) and marked tariffOnly; no part is a practice card of its own, because the scheme prices only the whole question.
sourceFindings: Páipéar I = 220: composition 120 (any two of A–D at 60: Tasc 3, Ábhar 9, Cumas Gaeilge 48) and reading 100 (A the weather and B Raidió Rí-Rá, five questions each at 10).

Reading (PDF 4): each question restated with one price and no answer. One 0–5 language deduction under each passage; after B the redundancy penalty (“[Gearrfar pionós i ngeall ar iomarcaíocht]”) and the Nóta on showing the marks; cards state them without applying them.
Composition (PDF 3–4): the examiner’s Nóta misprints “Tasc” as “Tásc”; kept as printed. No 48-mark table and no short-attempt columns.
